extDescription.message: See at a glance which Business Central environment you are in: your own colour in the top bar, frame, banner and tab icon.
extDescription.description: The description in the store listing. Hard limit of 132 characters, per language: a longer one is rejected at upload.

optionsTitle.description: Title of the options page. BC Buddy is a product name and stays as it is.

tagline.message: Tell your Business Central environments apart with colour, a frame and your own ribbon.
tagline.description: One-line summary under the title on the options page.

saveFailed.description: Shown when the settings could not be stored. $1 is the error message from the browser.

useOpenTabTitle.message: Takes the URL from an open tab, preferring a Business Central tab
useOpenTabTitle.description: Tooltip on the button next to the test URL.

noUsableTab.message: No open tab with a usable URL found.

labelRule.description: Column heading above the name of a rule.

labelEnvironment.description: Business Central term for the environment a tenant runs (production, sandbox). Use the word the Business Central UI uses in this language, not a literal translation.

labelCompany.description: Business Central term for a company inside an environment. Use the word the Business Central UI uses in this language.

labelTenant.description: Business Central term for the tenant the environment belongs to. Use the word the Business Central UI uses in this language.

rulesIntro.message: Which environment gets which colour. The first matching rule wins.

emptyRules.message: No rules yet. Click Add rule or import a configuration.

sharedIntro.message: Host a JSON file on a public HTTPS URL (e.g. a raw GitHub link) so everyone in the company uses the same markers.
sharedIntro.description: JSON, HTTPS and GitHub are names and stay as they are.

sharedTrust.message: Only use a URL you control (for example your team's repository). The file can define rules that mark any site.
sharedTrust.description: Warning about pointing the extension at a file somebody else controls.

syncFailed.description: $1 is the reason the download failed.

syncLoaded.description: $1 is a number of rules. The (s) is an English shortcut for the plural; use whatever the language really needs.

syncLoadedUnchanged.description: $1 is a number of rules. Unchanged means the file was the same as the last time it was fetched.

copiedToOwn.message: Copied $1 rule(s) to your own rules.
copiedToOwn.description: $1 is a number of rules copied out of the shared configuration into the user's own list.

statusSyncError.description: $1 is a date and time, $2 the error message.

statusHosted.description: $1 is a number of rules, $2 a date.

statusHostedNamed.description: $1 is a number of rules, $2 the name the shared file gives itself, $3 a date.

importIntro.message: From a file. Rules you already have are overwritten, new ones are added, and rules that are not in the file are left alone. This does not touch the shared configuration.

importFailed.description: $1 is the reason the import failed.

importDone.description: $1 is a number of rules, $2 the file name, $3 a summary put together from importOverwritten, importAdded and importKept.

importOverwritten.description: $1 is a number of rules. Ends up inside importDone, so it stays a fragment: no capital, no full stop.

importAdded.description: $1 is a number of rules. Ends up inside importDone, so it stays a fragment: no capital, no full stop.

importKept.description: $1 is a number of rules. Ends up inside importDone, so it stays a fragment: no capital, no full stop.

importNone.description: Stands in for the summary in importDone when the file changed nothing.

exportIntro.message: Exports your own rules only, in the format this extension also reads.

exportDone.description: $1 is a number of rules. bc-buddy.json is a file name and stays as it is.

ruleNamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the name field of a rule. TEST is an example of what somebody might call an environment.

ruleOn.description: Label on the on/off switch of a rule. Keep it short: the switch is narrow.

deleteConfirm.description: Asked before a rule is deleted. $1 is the name the user gave it.

matchYes.description: Shown on a rule that matches the test URL filled in above.

matchNo.message: Does not match the test URL
matchNo.description: Shown on a rule that does not match the test URL filled in above.

copySuffix.description: Name of a duplicated rule or layout. $1 is the name of the original.

previewPageBc.description: Caption on the mock Business Central page in the preview.

previewTitle.description: The name of a real Business Central page, shown on the mock page in the preview. Use the name that page has in this language.

conditionValuePlaceholder.message: e.g. Sandbox, CRONUS BE or a full URL
conditionValuePlaceholder.description: Examples of what a condition can look for. Sandbox is a Business Central term; CRONUS BE is the name of Microsoft's demo company and stays as it is.

conditionMatches.description: Choice in a condition: the rule applies when the condition is true.

conditionNoMatch.description: Choice in a condition: the rule applies when the condition is false.

fieldUrl.description: Part of the address a condition looks at. Stays URL in most languages.

fieldEnvironment.description: Business Central term for the environment a tenant runs (production, sandbox). Use the word the Business Central UI uses in this language.

fieldCompany.description: Business Central term for a company inside an environment. Use the word the Business Central UI uses in this language.

fieldTenant.description: Business Central term for the tenant the environment belongs to. Use the word the Business Central UI uses in this language.

opContains.description: Operator in a condition, read as one line: environment contains TEST. Lowercase on purpose, it sits in the middle of that line.

opEquals.description: Operator in a condition, read as one line: environment equals TEST. Lowercase on purpose, it sits in the middle of that line.

opStartsWith.description: Operator in a condition, read as one line: environment starts with TEST. Lowercase on purpose, it sits in the middle of that line.

opEndsWith.description: Operator in a condition, read as one line: environment ends with TEST. Lowercase on purpose, it sits in the middle of that line.

opRegex.description: Operator in a condition: match on a regular expression. Usually stays RegEx.

opNotContains.description: Operator in a condition, read as one line: environment does not contain TEST. Lowercase on purpose, it sits in the middle of that line.

displayHeading.description: Heading above everything that decides what a marked page looks like.

textAuto.description: Choice for the text colour: the extension picks black or white itself, whichever reads better on the chosen colour.

ribbonToggle.description: Switch for a diagonal coloured strip across a corner of the page. This is NOT the Office or Business Central ribbon toolbar: do not use that term.

ribbonText.description: The text printed on the diagonal corner strip, see ribbonToggle.

borderToggle.description: Switch for a coloured border drawn around the whole page.

borderWidth.description: Thickness of that border. px is a unit and stays as it is.

bannerToggle.description: Switch for a coloured bar with text along an edge of the page.

posBottom.description: Position of the banner: a full-width bar along the bottom of the page.

posTopRight.description: Position of the banner: a diagonal strip across the top right corner. Ribbon here means that strip, not a toolbar.

posTopLeft.description: Position of the banner: a diagonal strip across the top left corner. Ribbon here means that strip, not a toolbar.

posBottomRight.description: Position of the banner: a diagonal strip across the bottom right corner. Ribbon here means that strip, not a toolbar.

posBottomLeft.description: Position of the banner: a diagonal strip across the bottom left corner. Ribbon here means that strip, not a toolbar.

bannerText.description: The text on the banner, see bannerToggle.

bannerFontSize.description: Size of the banner text. Zero means the extension works it out itself.

titleToggle.description: Switch for replacing the title of the browser tab. The tab, not the Business Central page.

titleText.description: What the browser tab is called once titleToggle is on.

faviconToggle.description: Switch for replacing the small icon on the browser tab. Favicon is the usual word in most languages.

faviconLetters.description: The one or two letters drawn on that tab icon.

tokensAria.description: Opens the list of tokens, see tokensHeading.

tokensHeading.description: A token here is a placeholder the user types into a text, such as {name}, and the extension fills in. Nothing to do with a security token.

tokenName.description: Explains the {name} token, see tokensHeading. Lowercase: it is read after the token itself.

tokenEnvironment.description: Explains the {environment} token, see tokensHeading. Lowercase: it is read after the token itself.

tokenCompany.description: Explains the {company} token, see tokensHeading. Lowercase: it is read after the token itself.

tokenTitle.description: Explains the {title} token, see tokensHeading. Lowercase: it is read after the token itself.

tokensFooter.message: A token that stays empty disappears together with the separator next to it.
tokensFooter.description: Closing line under the list of tokens.

tokenOr.description: Joins two token names that mean the same thing, as in {name} or {rule}.

popupOwnRule.description: Says where the rule in force came from. A fragment that follows other text, hence lowercase.

popupShared.description: Says where the rule in force came from. A fragment that follows other text, hence lowercase.

popupNotBc.description: Shown in the popup when the tab is not a Business Central page.

syncShort.description: Short form of syncNow for the popup, where the button is narrow.

errHttpsOnly.message: The shared file must be served over HTTPS.
errHttpsOnly.description: HTTPS is a protocol name and stays as it is.

errHttp.description: $1 is an HTTP status code, $2 the status text that came with it.

clearSharedConfirm.message: Remove the $1 shared rules and switch the shared configuration off? The URL stays, so one click on Synchronise brings them back.
clearSharedConfirm.description: $1 is a number of rules. Synchronise is the button labelled syncNow: use the same wording.

errTimeout.message: The shared file did not respond within $1 seconds.

errTooLarge.message: The shared file is too large (limit $1 kB).

errInvalidJson.description: $1 is the error from the parser. JSON is a format name and stays as it is.

errNoRules.description: The word rules between quotes is a key in the file itself and stays in English.

errOtherApp.message: This file belongs to another application ($1).
errOtherApp.description: $1 is the name of the application the file says it belongs to.

importLayouts.description: Appended to importDone, which is why it starts with a space. $1 is a number of layouts, see layoutsHeading.

emptyLayouts.message: No layouts yet. Add one to reuse the same appearance across several rules.

layoutsIntro.message: What a marker looks like: ribbon, frame, banner, tab title and favicon.
layoutsIntro.description: Explains what a layout holds, see layoutsHeading.

deleteLayoutConfirm.message: Delete layout "$1"? $2 rule(s) will fall back to their own settings.
deleteLayoutConfirm.description: $1 is the name of the layout, $2 a number of rules that were using it.

layoutsHeading.description: A layout here is this extension's own idea: a saved set of appearance settings that several rules can share. It is not a Business Central report layout.

newLayoutName.description: The name a freshly added layout gets, see layoutsHeading.

copiedLayouts.description: Appended to copiedToOwn, which is why it starts with a space. $1 is a number of layouts.

layoutPreviewNote.message: Sample colour; every rule keeps its own.

layoutLabel.description: Label on the field that picks a layout for a rule, see layoutsHeading.

layoutNamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the name field of a layout. Default is an example of what somebody might call one.

navEnvironments.description: Navigation item leading to the rules, one per Business Central environment.

defaultLayoutName.description: The name of the layout that is there from the start. A name somebody sees in a list, not the word standard as a setting.

lastLayout.message: The last layout cannot be removed: there must always be one.
lastLayout.description: Shown when somebody tries to delete the only layout left.

aboutIntro.message: BC Buddy gives every Business Central environment its own colour: ribbon, frame, banner, tab title and favicon. One glance tells you whether you are in production, a sandbox or a demo, so you never change the wrong environment by accident.
aboutIntro.description: Business Central, production and sandbox are Business Central terms: use the words the Business Central UI uses in this language.

clearShared.message: Clear shared rules and stop updating
clearShared.description: Button that throws away the shared rules and stops the daily update.

sharedCleared.message: Shared rules cleared. They are no longer updated.

copyShared.message: Make your own copy of this rule
copyShared.description: Turns a shared rule into a copy the user owns and can edit.
